# Theme-guide independent lifecycle join

## Prospective resume contract

- Packet: R3, the owner-funded Gallery Synthwave theme-guide reliability work.
- Need: the prepared raw collector checks its own output; memory attribution also
  needs an independent interpretation of target/session/frame/context/isolate events.
- Deliverable: a pure trace/checkpoint join with explicit live, shared, missing and
  retired membership; adversarial controls and synthetic integration through the
  actual guard and checkpoint modules. No runtime optimization or new app dependency.
- Inputs: main `9e8d5ba`, the retained `dc4bd2f` lifecycle instrument and unchanged
  ADR-0073/memory-v2 budgets. Preserve the existing stash, source and all failures.
- Authority: kit-owned code/docs, synthetic tests and reviewed commit/push. No live
  guide, consumer mutation, real data, daemon/global change or installation.
- Acceptance: derive relationships from raw command/response/event identities, not
  producer `ok`/status/target summaries. Refuse ambiguity and contradictory/missing
  evidence; explain replacements, shared isolates and retired observations. Detach
  never proves destruction or memory reclamation. Always retain attribution as
  not-verified and memory/full-contract completion false pending independent controls.
- Cost cap: one economical two-file implementer and one bounded independent reviewer;
  initial synthetic round plus at most two repairs per module, approximately45minutes.
  Freeze executed bytes before every round. Zero browser acquisitions in this change;
  later qualification keeps the fixed one-positive/one-retention-control cap.
- Return/owner: app-kit maintainer records the checker, tests, evidence and the next
  control acquisition in the existing v2 contract. No catalog-readiness promotion.

## Result

Implemented the pure `joinGuideLifecycle` checker and synthetic actual-module
integration. It independently joins raw command/response IDs, attachment generations,
policy-before-resume ordering, target discovery/inventories, complete frame trees,
loaders, live execution contexts and repeated isolate observations. Checkpoints must
be chronological/non-overlapping and cannot reuse reads. Shared isolates, unexplained
replacements and retired members stay unqualified. Cleanup after the last checkpoint
does not retroactively rewrite that endpoint. Inputs are not mutated.

The result separates `evidence_valid` and `live_membership_complete` from attribution:
the latter always remains `not-verified`; memory/full-contract completion is always
false. A structural flag alone must not authorize a downstream acceptance claim.
Boundary/type/size errors throw; contradictory observations return explicit reasons.
The input is bounded to50,000 events,16 checkpoints,64 reads/checkpoint and16MiB
serialized data; each observed frame tree is bounded to64 nodes. This is not an
authenticated receipt format or a universal CDP topology validator.

## Remaining boundary and next action

This increment cannot establish live-browser ownership completeness,
detached/native/GPU reclamation, successful native guide cycles, process costs or a
memory budget pass. Initial context observation is not proof of actual context birth;
detach is not destruction, and destruction is not memory reclamation. A future
measurement must use both structural flags/reasons and its separate runtime controls.

Under the unchanged [memory-v2 contract](fixtures/styleguide-performance/memory-v2-contract.md),
freeze the acquisition plus this checker and qualify one benign native-navigation
control and one separately hosted retained-allocation control before one guide cell.
Stop on unknown ownership/containment; do not launch the full matrix or infer a
memory pass from these synthetic results. Historical v1 failures, ADR-0073, budgets,
human A/B and all broader G1/G3/G4 gates remain unchanged. No consumer files/pins,
dependencies, installed tools, running services or default appearance changed.
